source.title: Towards Unifying Neural Architecture Space Exploration and Generalization

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary information are present; some PDF text and figures are flattened or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether NN-Mass tracks test accuracy across architectures, but it does not measure train–test gaps, random-label memorization, or the specific interventions and comparisons in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy versus NN-Mass and parameter count. These results concern generalization performance but do not measure the train–test gap or match a listed version. Cited results, including the Wide-ResNet comparison, are not treated as the study's own training results.
record.test_reason: The study measures associations between network topology, gradient propagation and test accuracy, but tests none of V1–V8. Its width comparisons do not establish zero training error or examine widening beyond interpolation; its MLP and CNN experiments do not compare architectures on matched image tasks. NN-Mass and initial Jacobian singular values do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or train–test gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors link NN-Mass theoretically to layerwise gradient propagation and empirically to similar training convergence and test accuracy, with width held comparable for DenseNet-type networks. They also use it to design compressed DenseNet-type and MobileNet-type models.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies DenseNet-type skip-connection topology and measures NN-Mass, gradient properties, and test accuracy; it does not test the claim's random-label or train–test-gap recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy-fit strength varies with dataset and width multiplier; parameter count fits poorly at width multiplier wm = 3.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the tested architecture families and width groups, NN-Mass identifies models with similar test accuracy despite different depths, parameter counts and computational costs; its reported accuracy-fit R² generally exceeds parameter counting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network topology summarized by NN-Mass can predict test accuracy better than parameter count within the tested architecture families and width groups.

record.problems: Several comparisons are conveyed through figures; some cited baselines are imported from prior work. The paper's reported fit statistics concern test accuracy, not the train–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the standard ResNet/Wide-ResNet or MobileNet-V2 comparisons: the text reports fit statistics and qualitative accuracy clustering, but some source accuracies are taken directly from cited work and the claim versions do not cover these comparisons. No rows for compression table entries because compression is not a listed version and the comparisons do not measure a train–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Whether widening beyond the width needed for zero training error continues lowering test error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and interventions on learned local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Dropout interventions, underfitting, training-set-size dependence and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps and its ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing high-memorization examples compared with removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's relation from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. Test accuracy alone is sufficient for several claim versions, but the required interventions or comparisons are absent here. No verdict is warranted for V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same networks.
The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
The specified convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence and measuring resulting test accuracy.
